hero.subtitle: Artisanal concrete coffee makers. A functional sculpture for those who see beauty in the pause.

Index.manifesto: Each CAFCO pour-over is a minimal structure, made to hold an everyday ritual. Concrete, wood, and glass come together in an object that isn't just useful — it is presence.

catalog.title: The Collection
catalog.desc: Two models, two scales. The same commitment to honesty of material and detail.

a01v60.name: Pour-over A01
a01v60.desc: Conceived as a functional sculpture, it was designed to share the coffee ritual with others — a piece that invites you to pause, converse, and be present. Robust, sober, and brutalist: the A01 is the beginning of the CAFCO collection and a reference to living architecture.

a01bag.name: Pour-over A01
a01bag.tagline: The first of its series and local favorite.
a01bag.desc: The same monolithic textured concrete base with a symmetrical shape and warm teak wood detail. This version includes a traditional handcrafted cloth bag — for those who prefer the traditional Costa Rican method of brewing coffee.

a02v60.name: Pour-over A02
a02v60.tagline: For those who don't like sharing their coffee.
a02v60.desc: The A02 was born as a more portable version, designed to accompany you wherever you are: at home, in the office, or any space where the coffee ritual still has its place. A functional sculpture for a single cup, a reminder that even in the everyday, design can hold the pause.

a02bag.name: Pour-over A02
a02bag.desc: Compact, functional, and with the same architectural presence as the A01. It maintains the concrete structure and warm wood detail, but on a lighter scale, featuring the cloth bag for the traditional Costa Rican method.

materials.title: It's all in the details
materials.desc: At CAFCO we value those small aspects that define the essence of an object: its texture, its weight, its real shape.
materials.m1d: High-performance mix with a textured finish. Each base has a unique hue — without hiding imperfections, without disguising the process. The honesty of the material is the pillar.
materials.m2d: Reforested Costa Rican wood, protected with a moisture-resistant professional-grade sealer. Its warm grain complements the coldness of the concrete with an organic contrast designed to last.
materials.m3d: Heat-resistant V60-style dripper with ribbed walls for uniform extraction. Alternative available: handcrafted cloth bag for the Costa Rican method.

brew.title: Your ritual, elevated
brew.desc: Four steps for a perfect cup with your CAFCO pour-over.
brew.s1d: Heat the water to about 93°C and preheat the cone while rinsing the filter to remove residual flavors.
brew.s2d: Add 15g of medium-ground coffee into the filter and level the bed with a gentle shake.
brew.s3d: Begin pouring the water in slow, steady, and controlled circles, completing the extraction in 3 minutes.
brew.s4d: Carefully remove the filter, serve in your favorite mug, and enjoy the honest taste of your coffee unhurried.

audience.title: Who is this object for?
audience.pos1: It's for those who enjoy coffee as a conscious act.
audience.pos2: For those who value details, design, materiality, and silence.
audience.pos3: For those who see beauty in the pause and character in simplicity.
audience.pos4: This object is for those who don't just want to make coffee, but design a moment.
audience.pos5: CAFCO is for those who choose what they buy like they choose what they think: with care.
audience.cta: If this resonates with you, CAFCO is your best choice.

testimonials.q1: It's more than a pour-over — it's a design piece that transforms my morning into a ritual. The quality of the concrete and wood is felt in every detail.
testimonials.a1: Carlos V. — San José, Costa Rica

story.title: Beauty lies in the simple, the true, and the well-crafted
story.p1: In architecture, the honesty of a material is something very few people can appreciate. That's why, at CAFCO, we value those small aspects that define the essence of an object: its texture, its weight, its true shape.
story.p2: Each piece is born from respect for what it is — without hiding imperfections, without disguising the process — because we believe that design can also be sincere.
